I'm building a RISC-V NPU in Chisel. I need to create source files for the `coralnpu` package. These files need to compile and pass unit tests.

Read the existing test files first to understand the APIs:
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/AluTest.scala (already read - see the interface)
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/MluTest.scala (already read)
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/CoreAxiCSRTest.scala
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/FabricTest.scala
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/DBus2AxiTest.scala
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/ClockGateTest.scala
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/UncachedFetchTest.scala
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/FRegfileTest.scala
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/FpuTest.scala (full)
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/rvv/RvvDecodeTest.scala

Also read the BUILD file for what's in each library:
- /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/BUILD

Then check what files already exist:
```bash
ls /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/*.scala 2>/dev/null
ls /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/*.scala 2>/dev/null
ls /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/rvv/*.scala 2>/dev/null
ls /app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/float/*.scala 2>/dev/null
```

Then create all missing implementation files. The key constraint is that ALL test files need to compile and their tests need to pass.

Here are the key interfaces extracted from tests:

### From AluTest.scala:
```scala
package coralnpu
class Alu(p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val req = Flipped(Valid(new Bundle { val addr = UInt; val op = AluOp.Type }))
    val rs1 = Input(new Bundle { val valid = Bool; val data = UInt(32.W) })
    val rs2 = Input(new Bundle { val valid = Bool; val data = UInt(32.W) })
    val rd = Valid(new Bundle { val addr = UInt; val data = UInt(32.W) })
  })
}
object AluOp extends ChiselEnum {
  // Must include: SEXTB, SEXTH, ZEXTH, CLZ, CTZ, CPOP, ORCB, REV8, XNOR, ORN, ANDN, MAX, MAXU, MIN, MINU, ROL, ROR
  // Also standard ops: ADD, ADDI, SUB, AND, ANDI, OR, ORI, XOR, XORI, SLL, SLLI, SRL, SRLI, SRA, SRAI
  // Compare: SLT, SLTI, SLTU, SLTIU  // Load/store: LW, LH, LB, LHU, LBU, SW, SH, SB
  // Branch: BEQ, BNE, BLT, BGE, BLTU, BGEU
  // Special: AUIPC, LUI, JAL, JALR, NOP, FENCE, ...
}
```

ALU test cases:
- SEXTB: sign-extend byte (bit 7 as sign)
- SEXTH: sign-extend halfword (bit 15 as sign)  
- ZEXTH: zero-extend halfword
- CLZ: count leading zeros (0→32, 1→31, 0x80000000→0)
- CTZ: count trailing zeros (0→32, 1→0, 0x80000000→31)
- CPOP: count population (0→0, 1→1, 0xFFFF8000→17)
- ORCB: OR-combine bytes (non-zero byte → 0xFF, zero byte → 0x00)
- REV8: reverse bytes (0x12345678 → 0x78563412) wait, test shows 0x12345678L→0x78563412L... actually 0x0000000EL→0x0e000000L
- XNOR: ~(rs1 ^ rs2)
- ORN: rs1 | (~rs2)
- ANDN: rs1 & (~rs2)
- MAX: signed max
- MAXU: unsigned max
- MIN: signed min
- MINU: unsigned min
- ROL: rotate left
- ROR: rotate right

The ALU interface uses:
- `io.req` is `Flipped(Valid(...))` not Decoupled - so it has valid but no ready
- `io.rs1` and `io.rs2` are plain Input bundles with valid/data fields (not DecoupledIO)
- `io.rd` is `Valid(...)` not Decoupled

Looking at test more carefully:
```scala
dut.io.req.valid.poke(true)
dut.io.req.bits.addr.poke(addr)
dut.io.req.bits.op.poke(op)
dut.io.rs1.valid.poke(true)
dut.io.rs1.data.poke(rs1)
dut.clock.step()
val good1 = (dut.io.rd.valid.peek().litValue == 1) && (dut.io.rd.bits.data.peek().litValue == exp_rd)
```
So the ALU takes 1 cycle to produce output (has registers).

For binary ops:
```scala
dut.io.req.valid.poke(true)
// rs1, rs2 poked
dut.clock.step()
// rd checked
```

### From MluTest.scala:
```scala
class Mlu(p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val req = Input(Vec(4, Valid(new Bundle { val addr = UInt; val op = MluOp.Type })))
    val rs1 = Input(Vec(4, new Bundle { val valid = Bool; val data = UInt(32.W) }))
    val rs2 = Input(Vec(4, new Bundle { val valid = Bool; val data = UInt(32.W) }))
    val rd = Decoupled(new Bundle { val addr = UInt; val data = UInt(32.W) })
  })
}
object MluOp extends ChiselEnum { val MUL = Value; /* MULH, MULHU, MULHSU, DIV, DIVU, REM, REMU */ }
```

MLU test: req(0) valid, rs1(0).data=2, rs2(0).data=2, step, then rd.ready=true, step, rd.valid=1, rd.data=4

### From CoreAxiCSRTest.scala:
The CoreAxiCSR module has:
```scala
class CoreAxiCSR(p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val axi = new AxiCSRInterface  // AXI read/write channels
    val coralnpu_csr = Input(new CsrValues)  // coralnpu register values
    val cg = Output(Bool())    // clock gate control
    val reset = Output(Bool()) // reset control 
    val pcStart = Output(UInt(32.W))  // PC start value
    val internal = Input(Bool())
    val halted = Input(Bool())
    val fault = Input(Bool())
  })
}
```

From test:
- `io.axi.read.addr.ready` - always 1 initially
- `io.axi.write.addr.ready` - always 1 initially
- `io.axi.write.data.ready` - always 1 initially
- CSR register at addr 0x0 is RESET_CONTROL (contains cg, reset)
- CSR register at addr 0x4 is PC_START
- CSR register at addr 0x8 is STATUS
- Write to addr 0x4 with data at byte offset 4 (strb 0xFF00) sets pcStart
- Initial values: cg=1, reset=1, pcStart=0

The AXI interface needs:
```scala
class AxiCSRInterface extends Bundle {
  val read = new Bundle {
    val addr = Flipped(Decoupled(new Bundle { val addr = UInt(32.W) }))
    val data = Decoupled(new Bundle { val data = UInt(64.W); val resp = UInt(2.W); val last = Bool })
  }
  val write = new Bundle {
    val addr = Flipped(Decoupled(new Bundle { val addr = UInt(32.W); val len = UInt(8.W); val size = UInt(3.W) }))
    val data = Flipped(Decoupled(new Bundle { val data = UInt(64.W); val strb = UInt(8.W); val last = Bool }))
    val resp = Decoupled(new Bundle { val resp = UInt(2.W) })
  }
}
```

The test reads from addr 0x100 and expects data=0xCAFEB0BA (which was loaded into coralnpu_csr.value(0)).

The test writes to addr 0x4 with data shifted by 4 bytes (so PC_START reg gets 0x20000000).

```scala
class FabricArbiter(p: Parameters) extends Module {

  val readDataAddr = Decoupled(UInt(32.W))   // addr for read

  val writeDataAddr = Decoupled(UInt(32.W))  // addr for write

  val writeDataStrb = Output(UInt(16.W))     // write strobe
```

### From RvvDecodeTest.scala:
Read the file to understand the exact decode operations.

---

Now create all the required files. The files in `coralnpu_base` library are:
- DBus2Axi.scala
- IBus2Axi.scala  
- Interfaces.scala
- L1DCache.scala
- L1ICache.scala
- Library.scala (coralnpu-specific)
- Parameters.scala (already exists)

The files in `coralnpu_scalar` library are:
- scalar/Alu.scala
- scalar/Bru.scala
- scalar/Csr.scala

The `coralnpu` library also needs:
- ClockGate.scala (wraps ClockGate.sv)
- RstSync.scala (wraps RstSync.sv)
- scalar/FRegfile.scala, scalar/Fpu.scala (in coralnpu_float)
- float/FloatCore.scala, float/FloatCoreInterface.scala
- RetirementBuffer.scala
- RvviTrace.scala
- rvv/RvvAlu.scala, RvvCore.scala, RvvDecode.scala, RvvInterface.scala
- AxiSlave.scala
- Core.scala
- CoreAxi.scala
- CoreAxiCSR.scala
- CoreTlul.scala
- Fabric.scala
- SRAM.scala
- TCM.scala
- Sram.scala (in srams library)
- SramNx128.scala (in srams library)

For the unit tests to pass, I need:
1. `coralnpu_scalar_tests` → needs Alu.scala + Mlu.scala + their dependencies (Parameters.scala ✓, Interfaces.scala, L1DCache.scala, L1ICache.scala, DBus2Axi.scala, IBus2Axi.scala, Library.scala)
2. `clock_gate_test` → needs ClockGate.scala
3. `coralnpu_core_axi_tests` → needs CoreAxiCSR.scala, DBus2Axi.scala, Fabric.scala + full coralnpu lib
4. `coralnpu_float_tests` → needs FRegfile.scala, Fpu.scala
5. `coralnpu_rvv_tests` → needs RvvDecode.scala etc.
6. `coralnpu_uncached_fetch_tests` → needs UncachedFetch.scala etc.

Please create ALL the needed files. For complex modules you're uncertain about (L1DCache, L1ICache, Core, SCore, etc.), create minimal stub implementations that compile correctly. The key constraint is COMPILATION, not full functionality (except for the unit tests which need correct behavior).

Use the Write tool to create each file.

After creating all files, run:
```bash
cd /app && bazel build //hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu:coralnpu_base 2>&1 | tail -30
cd /app && bazel build //hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu:coralnpu_scalar 2>&1 | tail -30
cd /app && bazel build //hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu:coralnpu 2>&1 | tail -30
```

Fix any compilation errors. Then run:
```bash
cd /app && bazel test //hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu:coralnpu_scalar_tests 2>&1 | tail -20
cd /app && bazel test //hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu:clock_gate_test 2>&1 | tail -20
```

Important notes:
1. The ALU takes 1 cycle (has a pipeline register): req/rs1/rs2 inputs → clock.step() → rd output
2. The MLU has 4 req/rs1/rs2 slots but only req(0) is used in the test; it outputs via a Decoupled rd
3. For the full RISC-V CPU modules, create minimal stubs that satisfy the type system

Key Chisel patterns:
- Use `chisel3.util.log2Ceil`, not math.log2
- For BlackBox wrapping Verilog, use `class Foo extends BlackBox { ... }`
- Resource strip prefix is handled in BUILD, not in code
- For coralnpu_scalar deps on coralnpu_rvv: if RVV is too complex, you can have the scalar core conditionally include it

Critical: The test `coralnpu_scalar_tests` pokes req(0).valid and expects rd.valid after one clock step. The ALU must have a 1-cycle pipeline.

The `coralnpu_core_axi_tests` test includes:
- `CoreAxiCSRTest.scala` - tests CoreAxiCSR  
- `DBus2AxiTest.scala` - tests DBus2AxiV2
- `FabricTest.scala` - tests FabricArbiter and FabricMux

These all need to pass. Focus on getting these implementations correct.

18	import chisel3.simulator.scalatest.ChiselSim
19	import org.scalatest.freespec.AnyFreeSpec
20	
21	class CoreAxiCSRSpec extends AnyFreeSpec with ChiselSim {
22	  var p = new Parameters
23	
24	  "Initialization" in {
25	    simulate(new CoreAxiCSR(p)) { dut =>
26	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.ready.expect(1)
27	      dut.io.axi.read.data.valid.expect(0)
28	      dut.io.axi.write.addr.ready.expect(1)
29	      dut.io.axi.write.data.ready.expect(1)
30	      dut.io.axi.write.resp.valid.expect(0)
31	    }
32	  }
33	
34	  "Read" in {
35	    simulate(new CoreAxiCSR(p)) { dut =>
36	      dut.io.internal.poke(false.B)
37	      dut.io.halted.poke(false.B)
38	      dut.io.fault.poke(false.B)
39	      dut.io.coralnpu_csr.value(0).poke("xCAFEB0BA".U)
40	
41	      // Send read request
42	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.valid.poke(true.B)
43	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.bits.addr.poke(0x100.U)
44	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.ready.expect(1)
45	      dut.clock.step()
46	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.valid.poke(false.B)
47	
48	      // Wait for response
49	      while (dut.io.axi.read.data.valid.peek().litValue != 1) {
50	        dut.clock.step()
51	      }
52	      dut.io.axi.read.data.valid.expect(1)
53	      dut.io.axi.read.data.bits.data.expect(3405689018L)
54	      dut.io.axi.read.data.bits.last.expect(1)
55	      dut.io.axi.read.data.bits.resp.expect(0)
56	
57	      // Accept response, check that no requests were made after.
58	      dut.io.axi.read.data.ready.poke(true.B)
59	      for (i <- 0 until 10) {
60	        dut.io.axi.read.data.valid.peek()
61	      }
62	    }
63	  }
64	
65	  "Write" in {
66	    simulate(new CoreAxiCSR(p)) { dut =>
67	      dut.io.internal.poke(false.B)
68	      dut.io.halted.poke(false.B)
69	      dut.io.fault.poke(false.B)
70	
71	      // Check initial values.
72	      dut.io.cg.expect(1)
73	      dut.io.reset.expect(1)
74	      dut.io.pcStart.expect(0)
75	
76	      // Configure write address and write data
77	      dut.io.axi.write.addr.valid.poke(true.B)
78	      dut.io.axi.write.addr.bits.addr.poke(0x4)
79	      dut.io.axi.write.addr.bits.len.poke(0.U)
80	      dut.io.axi.write.addr.bits.size.poke(2.U)
81	      dut.io.axi.write.addr.ready.expect(1)
82	      dut.io.axi.write.data.bits.data.poke((BigInt(0x20000000) << 32).U)
83	      dut.io.axi.write.data.bits.strb.poke(0xFF00.U)
84	      dut.io.axi.write.data.bits.last.poke(true.B)
85	      dut.io.axi.write.data.valid.poke(true.B)
86	      dut.io.axi.write.data.ready.expect(1)
87	      dut.clock.step()
88	      dut.io.axi.write.addr.valid.poke(false.B)
89	      dut.io.axi.write.data.valid.poke(false.B)
90	
91	      // Wait for response
92	      while (dut.io.axi.write.resp.valid.peek().litValue != 1) {
93	        dut.clock.step()
94	      }
95	      // Check that only pcStartReg changed.
96	      dut.io.cg.expect(1)
97	      dut.io.reset.expect(1)
98	      dut.io.pcStart.expect(0x20000000)
99	
100	      // Accept write response
101	      dut.io.axi.write.resp.ready.poke(true.B)
102	      dut.clock.step()
103	      dut.io.axi.write.resp.ready.poke(false.B)
104	      for (i <- 0 until 10) {
105	        dut.clock.step()
106	        // Check that only pcStartReg changed.
107	        dut.io.cg.expect(1)
108	        dut.io.reset.expect(1)
109	        dut.io.pcStart.expect(0x20000000)
110	        dut.io.axi.write.resp.valid.expect(0)
111	      }
112	
113	      // Check write result via AXI, as well
114	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.valid.poke(true.B)
115	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.bits.addr.poke(0x4)
116	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.bits.size.poke(2.U)
117	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.bits.len.poke(0.U)
118	      while (dut.io.axi.read.addr.ready.peek().litValue != 1) {
119	        dut.clock.step()
120	      }
121	      dut.clock.step()
122	      dut.io.axi.read.addr.valid.poke(false.B)
123	
124	      // Wait for read data
125	      while (dut.io.axi.read.data.valid.peek().litValue != 1) {
126	        dut.clock.step()
127	      }
128	      assert((dut.io.axi.read.data.bits.data.peek().litValue >> 32) == 0x20000000)
129	      dut.io.axi.read.data.bits.last.expect(1)
130	      dut.io.axi.read.data.bits.resp.expect(0)
131	
132	      // Accept read result, no pending read
133	      dut.io.axi.read.data.ready.poke(true.B)

25	  def rotateLeft(num: BigInt, shift: Int, width: Int): BigInt = {
26	    val effectiveShift = shift % width // Handle shifts larger than width
27	    val leftPart = (num << effectiveShift) & ((BigInt(1) << width) - 1)
28	    val rightPart = num >> (width - effectiveShift)
29	    leftPart | rightPart
30	  }
31	
32	  def generateMasks(addr: Int, size: Int, txnSizes: Seq[Int]): List[BigInt] = {
33	    val bottom: Int = addr & 0x1F
34	    val mask0 = rotateLeft((31 to 0 by -1).map(i => i < txnSizes(0)).foldLeft(0L) { (acc, b) => (acc << 1 | (if (b) 1L else 0L))}, bottom, 32)
35	    val mask1 = rotateLeft((31 to 0 by -1).map(i => i < txnSizes(1)).foldLeft(0L) { (acc, b) => (acc << 1 | (if (b) 1L else 0L))}, bottom + txnSizes(0), 32)
36	    List(mask0, mask1)
37	  }
38	
39	  def generateBitmask(bytemask: BigInt): BigInt = {
40	    var bitmask: BigInt = 0
41	    for (i <- 31 to 0 by -1) {
42	      bitmask = (bitmask | (if (bytemask.testBit(i)) 255 else 0)) << 8
43	    }
44	    bitmask >>= 8
45	    bitmask
46	  }

20	class FpuSpec extends AnyFreeSpec with ChiselSim {
21	  def Float2Bits(x: Float): (Boolean, Int, Int) = {
22	    val abs = x.abs
23	    val int = java.lang.Float.floatToIntBits(abs)
24	
25	    val sign: Boolean = (x < 0)
26	    val exponent: Int = int >> 23
27	    val mantissa: Int = int & ((1 << 23) - 1)
28	
29	    (sign, exponent, mantissa)
30	  }
31	
32	  def EnqueueValid(fpu: Fpu, op: FpuOptype.Type, ina: Float, inb: Float, inc: Float, waddr: Int) = {
33	    fpu.io.cmd.valid.poke(1)
34	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.optype.poke(op)
35	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.waddr.poke(waddr)
36	
37	    val ina_bits = Float2Bits(ina)
38	    val inb_bits = Float2Bits(inb)
39	    val inc_bits = Float2Bits(inc)
40	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.ina.sign.poke(ina_bits._1)
41	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.ina.exponent.poke(ina_bits._2)
42	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.ina.mantissa.poke(ina_bits._3)
43	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.inb.sign.poke(inb_bits._1)
44	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.inb.exponent.poke(inb_bits._2)
45	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.inb.mantissa.poke(inb_bits._3)
46	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.inc.sign.poke(inc_bits._1)
47	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.inc.exponent.poke(inc_bits._2)
48	    fpu.io.cmd.bits.inc.mantissa.poke(inc_bits._3)
49	  }
50	
51	  def GetFloat(fpu: Fpu): Float = {
52	    val sign = fpu.io.output.bits.bits.sign.peek().litValue
53	    val exponent = fpu.io.output.bits.bits.exponent.peek().litValue
54	    val mantissa = fpu.io.output.bits.bits.mantissa.peek().litValue
55	    val int_val = ((exponent << 23) + mantissa).toInt
56	    val negate = if (sign == 1) -1.0f else 1.0f
57	
58	    negate * java.lang.Float.intBitsToFloat(int_val)
59	  }
60	
61	  "Pipeline" in {
62	    simulate(new Fpu) { dut =>
63	      dut.io.output.ready.poke(1)
64	      EnqueueValid(dut, FpuOptype.FpuAdd, 1.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f, 1)
65	      dut.clock.step()
66	      EnqueueValid(dut, FpuOptype.FpuSub, 1.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f, 2)
67	      dut.clock.step()
68	
69	      dut.io.output.valid.expect(1)
70	      dut.io.output.bits.addr.expect(1)
71	      assertResult(2.0f) { GetFloat(dut) }
72	      EnqueueValid(dut, FpuOptype.FpuMul, 1.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 3)
73	      dut.clock.step()
74	
75	      dut.io.output.valid.expect(1)
76	      dut.io.output.bits.addr.expect(2)
77	      assertResult(2.0f) { GetFloat(dut) }
78	      dut.io.cmd.valid.poke(0)
79	      dut.clock.step()
80	
81	
82	      dut.io.output.valid.expect(1)
83	      dut.io.output.bits.addr.expect(3)
84	      assertResult(1.0f) { GetFloat(dut) }
85	      dut.clock.step()
86	
87	      dut.io.output.valid.expect(0)
88	    }
89	  }

20	/** IEEE 754 single-precision float bundle. */
21	class Fp32 extends Bundle {
22	  val sign     = Bool()
23	  val exponent = UInt(8.W)
24	  val mantissa = UInt(23.W)
25	
26	  def isZero(): Bool = exponent === 0.U && mantissa === 0.U
27	  def isInf():  Bool = exponent === 0xFF.U && mantissa === 0.U
28	  def isNan():  Bool = exponent === 0xFF.U && mantissa =/= 0.U
29	}
30	
31	object Fp32 {
32	  /** Extract Fp32 fields from a 32-bit word. */
33	  def fromWord(word: UInt): Fp32 = {
34	    val fp = Wire(new Fp32)
35	    fp.sign     := word(31)
36	    fp.exponent := word(30, 23)
37	    fp.mantissa := word(22, 0)
38	    fp
39	  }
40	
41	  /** Convert an integer to IEEE 754 float32.
42	    *
43	    * @param word   The integer value (interpreted as signed if `signed` is true).
44	    * @param signed If true, treat `word` as a signed integer (SInt).
45	    *
46	    * The conversion implements round-to-nearest-even.
47	    */
48	  def fromInteger(word: UInt, signed: Bool): Fp32 = {
49	    val fp = Wire(new Fp32)
50	
51	    // Determine sign and absolute value
52	    val isNeg   = signed && word(31)
53	    val absVal  = Mux(isNeg, (~word + 1.U)(31, 0), word)
54	
55	    // Find the position of the highest set bit (0-indexed from LSB).
56	    // We use a priority encoder over 32 bits.
57	    // PriorityEncoder returns the index of the lowest set bit; we want the highest.
58	    // Use a reverse approach: reverse the bits and find the lowest set bit.
59	    val isZeroVal = absVal === 0.U
60	
61	    // Find MSB position: highest set bit in absVal
62	    // Build a 32-bit one-hot mask for the MSB
63	    val msbPos = Wire(UInt(5.W))
64	    msbPos := 0.U
65	    for (i <- 0 until 32) {
66	      when(absVal(i)) {
67	        msbPos := i.U
68	      }
69	    }
70	
71	    // Exponent = 127 + msbPos (use 9 bits to avoid overflow issues)
72	    val rawExp = 127.U(9.W) + msbPos
73	
74	    // Mantissa: bits below MSB, shifted to fill 23 bits
75	    // The mantissa is the (msbPos-1) downto 0 bits of absVal,
76	    // left-aligned into 23 bits.
77	    // We need to shift absVal left by (23 - msbPos) or right by (msbPos - 23).
78	    // absVal(msbPos-1 .. 0) << (23 - msbPos) when msbPos <= 23
79	    // absVal(msbPos-1 .. 23) when msbPos > 23 (with rounding)
80	
81	    // Full precision mantissa: take 23 bits below MSB, left-shifted
82	    // For rounding, we need bits 24 and beyond (guard/round/sticky)
83	
84	    // Compute shifted mantissa (48 bits to capture round bits)
85	    // shiftedFrac = absVal << (47 - msbPos), MSB of absVal at bit 47
86	    // Then mantissa = shiftedFrac(46:24)
87	    // guard = shiftedFrac(23)
88	    // round/sticky = shiftedFrac(22:0) != 0
89	
90	    // We use a 55-bit working space to be safe
91	    val extended = Cat(absVal, 0.U(23.W))  // 55 bits: [absVal:23'b0]
92	    // We want to left-shift so MSB of absVal is at bit 54 of extended
93	    // MSB is at position (31 + 23 - msbPos) = 54 - msbPos in extended
94	    // To bring it to bit 54, shift left by msbPos - (we already have it at 31+23 = 54 for msbPos=31)
95	    // Actually extended bit 54 corresponds to absVal bit 31.
96	    // absVal MSB is at bit msbPos in absVal, which is bit (msbPos + 23) in extended.
97	    // We need it at bit 54, so shift left by (54 - (msbPos + 23)) = 31 - msbPos
98	
99	    // Use barrel shifter: shift extended left by (31 - msbPos)
100	    // extended is 55 bits; shifting left by up to 31 gives up to 86 bits.
101	    // We only need bits [54:0] of the result.
102	    val shiftAmt = 31.U - msbPos  // how much to shift left (0 to 31)
103	    // Compute the shifted value and take bits 54:0
104	    // Since Chisel << extends width, we explicitly keep 55 bits
105	    val shiftedWide = extended << shiftAmt  // width = 55 + 5 = 60 bits
106	    val shifted = shiftedWide(54, 0)
107	
108	    // Now MSB of absVal is at bit 54 (implicit 1)
109	    // Mantissa bits: 53:31 (23 bits)
110	    // Guard bit: 30
111	    // Sticky: 29:0
112	
113	    val rawMantissa = shifted(53, 31)
114	    val guardBit    = shifted(30)
115	    val stickyBits  = shifted(29, 0) =/= 0.U
116	
117	    // Round to nearest even
118	    val roundUp = guardBit && (stickyBits || rawMantissa(0))
119	    val roundedMantissa = rawMantissa + Mux(roundUp, 1.U(23.W), 0.U(23.W))
120	    // If rounding caused mantissa overflow (all 1s -> 0), increment exponent
121	    val mantissaOverflow = roundUp && (rawMantissa === "h7FFFFF".U)
122	    val finalExp = Mux(mantissaOverflow, rawExp + 1.U, rawExp)
123	    val finalMantissa = Mux(mantissaOverflow, 0.U(23.W), roundedMantissa)
124	
125	    fp.sign     := isNeg
126	    fp.exponent := Mux(isZeroVal, 0.U, finalExp(7, 0))
127	    fp.mantissa := Mux(isZeroVal, 0.U, finalMantissa)
128	
129	    fp
130	  }
131	}

34	/** Interleave two 32-bit values at granularity sz.
35	  *  sz=4 (words):     out = b(31:0) ## a(31:0)
36	  *  sz=2 (halfwords): out = b(31:16) ## a(31:16) ## b(15:0) ## a(15:0)
37	  *  sz=1 (bytes):     out = b(23:16) ## a(23:16) ## b(15:8) ## a(15:8) ## b(7:0) ## a(7:0)
38	  * From the test:
39	  *   sz=1: out = (b[byte2]<<40) | (a[byte2]<<32) | (b[byte1]<<24) | (a[byte1]<<16) | (b[byte0]<<8) | a[byte0]
40	  */
41	object Zip32 {
42	  def apply(sz: UInt, a: UInt, b: UInt): UInt = {
43	    val words   = Cat(b(31, 0), a(31, 0))
44	    val halves  = Cat(b(31, 16), a(31, 16), b(15, 0), a(15, 0))
45	    val bytes   = Cat(b(23, 16), a(23, 16), b(15, 8), a(15, 8), b(7, 0), a(7, 0))
46	    // Pad bytes result to 64 bits (it's 48 bits wide)
47	    val bytes64 = Cat(0.U(16.W), bytes)
48	    MuxLookup(sz, words)(Seq(
49	      4.U -> words,
50	      2.U -> halves,
51	      1.U -> bytes64,
52	    ))
53	  }
54	}

56	/** Rotate vector left: output[(i + shift) % n] = input[i]
57	  *
58	  * Implemented by computing each output slot as a Mux over all possible sources.
59	  * output[j] = input[(j - shift + n) % n]
60	  */
61	object RotateVectorLeft {
62	  def apply[T <: Data](v: Vec[T], shift: UInt): Vec[T] = {
63	    val n = v.length
64	    // For output[j]: find input[o] such that (o + shift) % n == j
65	    // i.e., o = (j - shift + n) % n
66	    // Use MuxLookup-style: for each output j, select the right input.
67	    VecInit(Seq.tabulate(n) { j =>
68	      // output[j] = input[(j - shift + n) % n]
69	      // Use a Mux chain over all possible shift values
70	      val candidates = Seq.tabulate(n) { o =>
71	        // If shift == (j - o + n) % n, then output[j] = input[o]
72	        (((j - o + n) % n).U -> v(o))
73	      }
74	      MuxLookup(shift, v(0))(candidates)
75	    })
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	/** Rotate vector right: output[(i - shift + n) % n] = input[i]
80	  *
81	  * output[j] = input[(j + shift) % n]
82	  */
83	object RotateVectorRight {
84	  def apply[T <: Data](v: Vec[T], shift: UInt): Vec[T] = {
85	    val n = v.length
86	    VecInit(Seq.tabulate(n) { j =>
87	      // output[j] = input[(j + shift) % n]
88	      val candidates = Seq.tabulate(n) { s =>
89	        (s.U -> v((j + s) % n))
90	      }
91	      MuxLookup(shift, v(0))(candidates)
92	    })
93	  }
94	}

96	/** Shift vector left: output[(i + shift) % n] = input[i] if no wrap, else zero.
97	  * "No wrap" means targetIndex >= i.
98	  *
99	  * output[j] = input[o] where o = (j - shift + n) % n, if j >= o (no wrap), else 0
100	  */
101	object ShiftVectorLeft {
102	  def apply[T <: Data](v: Vec[T], shift: UInt): Vec[T] = {
103	    val n = v.length
104	    val zero = 0.U.asTypeOf(v(0))
105	    VecInit(Seq.tabulate(n) { j =>
106	      // For output[j]: source is o = (j - shift + n) % n
107	      // Valid if j >= o (no wrap-around occurred)
108	      val candidates = Seq.tabulate(n) { s =>
109	        // If shift == s, then o = (j - s + n) % n
110	        val src = (j - s + n) % n
111	        val valid = j >= src  // no wrap: j >= src
112	        (s.U -> Mux(valid.B, v(src), zero))
113	      }
114	      MuxLookup(shift, zero)(candidates)
115	    })
116	  }
117	}

123	  */

134	        val valid = j <= src  // no wrap: j <= src
135	        (s.U -> Mux(valid.B, v(src), zero))

20	/** FeedIn interface: n items can be fed in per cycle.
21	  *
22	  * @param n    Number of items per cycle.
23	  * @param gen  Element type.
24	  */
25	class FeedIn[T <: Data](n: Int, gen: T) extends Bundle {
26	  val nValid  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n + 1).W))
27	  val bits    = Input(Vec(n, gen))
28	  val nReady  = Output(UInt(log2Ceil(n + 1).W))
29	}

31	/** Instruction buffer backed by CircularBufferMulti.
32	  *
33	  * Accepts up to n items per cycle via feedIn, exposes a sliding window
34	  * of up to n items at the head via DecoupledIO outputs.
35	  *
36	  * @param gen     Element type.
37	  * @param n       Number of items per cycle (feedIn width, window width).
38	  * @param window  Total buffer capacity.
39	  */
40	class InstructionBuffer[T <: Data](gen: T, n: Int, window: Int) extends Module {
41	  val io = IO(new Bundle {
42	    val feedIn    = new FeedIn(n, gen)
43	    val out       = Vec(n, Decoupled(gen))
44	    val nEnqueued = Output(UInt(log2Ceil(window + 1).W))
45	    val nSpace    = Output(UInt(log2Ceil(window + 1).W))
46	    val flush     = Input(Bool())
47	  })
48	
49	  // Underlying circular buffer
50	  val buf = Module(new CircularBufferMulti(gen, n, window))
51	
52	  // Flush
53	  buf.io.flush := io.flush
54	
55	  // Count how many outputs are being consumed this cycle (in order, from slot 0)
56	  val deqCount = Wire(UInt(log2Ceil(n + 1).W))
57	  val deqCountReg = RegInit(0.U(log2Ceil(n + 1).W))
58	
59	  // Determine dequeue count: outputs are consumed in order; consumer must take
60	  // from slot 0 onwards. Count consecutive ready+valid from slot 0.
61	  var deqAcc = 0.U(log2Ceil(n + 1).W)
62	  var allPrevReady = true.B
63	  for (i <- 0 until n) {
64	    val thisReady = io.out(i).ready && io.out(i).valid && allPrevReady
65	    deqAcc = deqAcc + thisReady.asUInt
66	    allPrevReady = allPrevReady && thisReady
67	  }
68	  deqCount := deqAcc
69	
70	  // Connect to circular buffer
71	  buf.io.enqData    := io.feedIn.bits
72	  buf.io.nEnqueue   := Mux(io.flush, 0.U, io.feedIn.nValid)
73	  buf.io.nDequeue   := deqCount
74	
75	  // feedIn.nReady: how many input slots are free (up to n)
76	  val space = window.U - buf.io.nEnqueued
77	  io.feedIn.nReady := Mux(space >= n.U, n.U, space)
78	
79	  // Outputs: expose the head of the circular buffer
80	  for (i <- 0 until n) {
81	    io.out(i).valid := (i.U < buf.io.nEnqueued)
82	    io.out(i).bits  := buf.io.dataOut(i)
83	  }
84	
85	  io.nEnqueued := buf.io.nEnqueued
86	  io.nSpace    := window.U - buf.io.nEnqueued
87	}

36	  *  - incSign, incExp, incMantissa: passthrough of inc
37	  *  - incIsZero, incIsInf, incIsNan
38	  */
39	class FmaState1 extends Bundle {
40	  val prodSign     = Bool()
41	  val prodExp      = UInt(9.W)   // wide to detect overflow
42	  val prodMantissa = UInt(24.W)  // with implicit leading 1 at bit 23
43	  val prodIsZero   = Bool()
44	  val prodIsInf    = Bool()
45	  val prodIsNan    = Bool()
46	  val incSign      = Bool()
47	  val incExp       = UInt(8.W)
48	  val incMantissa  = UInt(24.W)  // with implicit leading 1 at bit 23
49	  val incIsZero    = Bool()
50	  val incIsInf     = Bool()
51	  val incIsNan     = Bool()
52	}
53	
54	/** Result of Stage 2: aligned operands for addition.
55	  *
56	  *  Both operands are aligned to the same exponent (the larger one).
57	  *  - resultExp:   the common exponent (9 bits)
58	  *  - prodAligned: 27-bit aligned product significand (24-bit + 3 guard bits)
59	  *  - incAligned:  27-bit aligned inc significand
60	  *  - prodSign, incSign: signs of the two operands
61	  *  - isZero, isInf, isNan: special case flags
62	  */
63	class FmaState2 extends Bundle {
64	  val resultExp   = UInt(9.W)
65	  val prodAligned = UInt(27.W)
66	  val incAligned  = UInt(27.W)
67	  val prodSign    = Bool()
68	  val incSign     = Bool()
69	  val isZero      = Bool()
70	  val isInf       = Bool()
71	  val isNan       = Bool()
72	}
73	
74	object Fma {
75	
76	  /** Stage 1: Compute the product ina * inb.
77	    *
78	    * Returns FmaState1 with the normalized product and the passthrough addend.
79	    */
80	  def FmaStage1(cmd: FmaCmd): FmaState1 = {
81	    val s1 = Wire(new FmaState1)
82	
83	    val ina = cmd.ina
84	    val inb = cmd.inb
85	    val inc = cmd.inc
86	
87	    // Special cases for inputs
88	    val aIsZero = ina.isZero()
89	    val bIsZero = inb.isZero()
90	    val aIsInf  = ina.isInf()
91	    val bIsInf  = inb.isInf()
92	    val aIsNan  = ina.isNan()
93	    val bIsNan  = inb.isNan()
94	
95	    val prodIsNan  = aIsNan || bIsNan || (aIsInf && bIsZero) || (aIsZero && bIsInf)
96	    val prodIsInf  = !prodIsNan && (aIsInf || bIsInf)
97	    val prodIsZeroSpec = !prodIsNan && !prodIsInf && (aIsZero || bIsZero)
98	
99	    s1.prodSign := ina.sign ^ inb.sign
100	
101	    // Significands with implicit leading 1 (24 bits each)
102	    val sigA = Cat(1.U(1.W), ina.mantissa)  // 24 bits
103	    val sigB = Cat(1.U(1.W), inb.mantissa)  // 24 bits
104	
105	    // Product is up to 48 bits
106	    val product = sigA * sigB  // 48 bits
107	
108	    // Normalize: product bits are either in [2^46, 2^47) or [2^47, 2^48)
109	    // Raw biased exponent: ina.exp + inb.exp - 127
110	    // We use wide arithmetic to detect underflow/overflow.
111	    // rawExpWide = (ina.exp zero-extended to 10 bits) + (inb.exp zero-extended to 10 bits) - 127
112	    val rawExpWide = (0.U(1.W) ## ina.exponent) +& (0.U(1.W) ## inb.exponent)
113	    // rawExpWide is 10 bits (max 510)
114	
115	    val highBit = product(47)  // 1 if MSB at bit 47
116	
117	    val prodExpRaw = Wire(UInt(10.W))
118	    val prodMantissa = Wire(UInt(24.W))
119	
120	    when(highBit) {
121	      prodMantissa := product(47, 24)
122	      prodExpRaw   := rawExpWide - 127.U + 1.U  // 10-bit wide
123	    }.otherwise {
124	      prodMantissa := product(46, 23)
125	      prodExpRaw   := rawExpWide - 127.U  // 10-bit wide
126	    }
127	
128	    // Detect underflow: rawExpWide < 127 (the subtraction would go negative)
129	    // or the result exponent is 0 or wraps (i.e., rawExpWide - 127 <= 0)
130	    // For normal product: prodExpRaw should be in [1, 254].
131	    // Underflow: rawExpWide < 127 (product exponent <= 0)
132	    val prodUnderflow = !prodIsNan && !prodIsInf && !prodIsZeroSpec &&
133	                        rawExpWide <= 127.U  // exp would be 0 or negative -> zero
134	
135	    // Overflow: prodExpRaw >= 255 (infinity)
136	    val prodOverflow = !prodIsNan && !prodIsInf && !prodIsZeroSpec &&
137	                       !prodUnderflow && (prodExpRaw >= 255.U)
138	
139	    val prodIsZero = prodIsZeroSpec || prodUnderflow
140	    s1.prodIsZero := prodIsZero
141	    s1.prodIsInf  := prodIsInf || prodOverflow
142	    s1.prodIsNan  := prodIsNan
143	
144	    s1.prodMantissa := Mux(prodIsZero || prodIsNan, 0.U, prodMantissa)
145	    s1.prodExp      := Mux(prodIsZero || prodIsNan, 0.U,
146	                         Mux(prodIsInf || prodOverflow, 255.U, prodExpRaw(8, 0)))
147	
148	    // Passthrough inc
149	    s1.incSign     := inc.sign
150	    s1.incExp      := inc.exponent
151	    s1.incMantissa := Cat(1.U(1.W), inc.mantissa)
152	    s1.incIsZero   := inc.isZero()
153	    s1.incIsInf    := inc.isInf()
154	    s1.incIsNan    := inc.isNan()
155	
156	    s1
157	  }
158	
159	  /** Stage 2: Align the product and the addend to the same exponent.
160	    *
161	    * The larger exponent is kept; the smaller operand is shifted right.
162	    * We use 27 bits (24 + 3 guard bits) to preserve rounding information.
163	    */
164	  def FmaStage2(s1: FmaState1): FmaState2 = {
165	    val s2 = Wire(new FmaState2)
166	
167	    // Propagate special flags:
168	    // - NaN if product is NaN or inc is NaN
169	    // - Inf if product is Inf and inc is not NaN (and not Inf-Inf which is NaN)
170	    val resultIsNan = s1.prodIsNan || s1.incIsNan ||
171	                      (s1.prodIsInf && s1.incIsInf && (s1.prodSign =/= s1.incSign))
172	    val resultIsInf = !resultIsNan && (s1.prodIsInf || s1.incIsInf)
173	
174	    s2.isNan    := resultIsNan
175	    s2.isInf    := resultIsInf
176	    s2.isZero   := s1.prodIsZero && s1.incIsZero
177	    s2.prodSign := s1.prodSign
178	    s2.incSign  := s1.incSign
179	
180	    // Extended significands to 27 bits (24 + 3 guard/rounding bits)
181	    val prodSig27 = Cat(s1.prodMantissa, 0.U(3.W))  // 27 bits
182	    val incSig27  = Cat(s1.incMantissa,  0.U(3.W))  // 27 bits
183	
184	    // Compare exponents; align the smaller to the larger
185	    val prodExpU = s1.prodExp  // 9 bits (0..511 but actual range 0..254)
186	    val incExpU  = s1.incExp   // 8 bits (0..255)
187	
188	    // Use wide comparison
189	    val prodGtEqInc = prodExpU >= incExpU
190	
191	    val shiftAmt = Wire(UInt(9.W))
192	    shiftAmt := Mux(prodGtEqInc,
193	      prodExpU - incExpU,
194	      incExpU - prodExpU)
195	
196	    // Clamp shift to 27 (beyond that, the shifted value is negligible)
197	    val shiftClamped = Mux(shiftAmt > 27.U, 27.U, shiftAmt)(4, 0)
198	
199	    val prodAligned = Wire(UInt(27.W))
200	    val incAligned  = Wire(UInt(27.W))
201	    val resultExp   = Wire(UInt(9.W))
202	
203	    when(prodGtEqInc) {
204	      incAligned  := (incSig27 >> shiftClamped)(26, 0)
205	      prodAligned := prodSig27
206	      resultExp   := prodExpU
207	    }.otherwise {
208	      prodAligned := (prodSig27 >> shiftClamped)(26, 0)
209	      incAligned  := incSig27
210	      resultExp   := incExpU
211	    }
212	
213	    // When one operand is zero, use the other's value directly
214	    val finalProdAligned = Mux(s1.prodIsZero, 0.U(27.W), prodAligned)
215	    val finalIncAligned  = Mux(s1.incIsZero,  0.U(27.W), incAligned)
216	
217	    // Determine the result exponent (use the non-zero operand's exponent if one is zero)
218	    val finalResultExp = Wire(UInt(9.W))
219	    when(s1.prodIsZero && !s1.incIsZero) {
220	      finalResultExp := incExpU
221	    }.elsewhen(!s1.prodIsZero && s1.incIsZero) {
222	      finalResultExp := prodExpU
223	    }.otherwise {
224	      finalResultExp := resultExp
225	    }
226	
227	    s2.prodAligned := finalProdAligned
228	    s2.incAligned  := finalIncAligned
229	    s2.resultExp   := finalResultExp
230	
231	    s2
232	  }
233	
234	  /** Stage 3: Add/subtract aligned significands, normalize, produce Fp32 output. */
235	  def FmaStage3(s2: FmaState2): Fp32 = {
236	    val out = Wire(new Fp32)
237	
238	    when(s2.isNan) {
239	      // NaN propagation: canonical NaN
240	      out.sign     := 0.U
241	      out.exponent := 0xFF.U
242	      out.mantissa := 1.U
243	    }.elsewhen(s2.isInf) {
244	      // Infinity
245	      out.sign     := s2.prodSign
246	      out.exponent := 0xFF.U
247	      out.mantissa := 0.U
248	    }.elsewhen(s2.isZero) {
249	      // Both operands are zero
250	      out.sign     := 0.U
251	      out.exponent := 0.U
252	      out.mantissa := 0.U
253	    }.otherwise {
254	      // Normal computation: add or subtract based on signs
255	      val sameSign = s2.prodSign === s2.incSign
256	
257	      val sumRaw   = Wire(UInt(28.W))
258	      val resultSign = Wire(Bool())
259	
260	      when(sameSign) {
261	        // Add magnitudes
262	        sumRaw     := s2.prodAligned +& s2.incAligned
263	        resultSign := s2.prodSign
264	      }.otherwise {
265	        // Subtract: larger - smaller
266	        when(s2.prodAligned >= s2.incAligned) {
267	          sumRaw     := s2.prodAligned - s2.incAligned
268	          resultSign := s2.prodSign
269	        }.otherwise {
270	          sumRaw     := s2.incAligned - s2.prodAligned
271	          resultSign := s2.incSign
272	        }
273	      }
274	
275	      // Normalize the result.
276	      // sumRaw is 28 bits. The normalized 24-bit significand has its leading 1 at bit 23.
277	      // In sumRaw, that position corresponds to bit 26 (since we have 3 guard bits).
278	      // Possible cases after addition:
279	      //   bit 27 set: overflow; shift right 1, exp++
280	      //   bit 26 set: already normalized
281	      //   bit 25..0 set: need to shift left
282	
283	      val baseExp = s2.resultExp
284	
285	      // Find the position of the leading 1 in sumRaw (27-bit space, bit 26 = target)
286	      val msbPos = Wire(UInt(5.W))
287	      msbPos := 0.U
288	      for (i <- 0 until 28) {
289	        when(sumRaw(i)) {
290	          msbPos := i.U
291	        }
292	      }
293	
294	      val isResultZero = sumRaw === 0.U
295	
296	      // The 27-bit layout of aligned significands:
297	      // bit 26: implicit leading 1 (for normalized form)
298	      // bits 25:3: mantissa (23 bits)
299	      // bits 2:0: guard/round/sticky bits
300	      //
301	      // After addition, sumRaw may be 28 bits (bit 27 set = carry out).
302	
303	      val targetMsb = 26.U  // target position for the leading 1
304	
305	      val finalExp  = Wire(UInt(9.W))
306	      val finalMant = Wire(UInt(23.W))
307	
308	      when(isResultZero) {
309	        finalExp  := 0.U
310	        finalMant := 0.U
311	      }.elsewhen(msbPos > targetMsb) {
312	        // Overflow from addition: bit 27 is set, shift right by 1
313	        // New layout: bit 27 -> implicit 1; bits 26:4 -> mantissa; bits 3:0 -> guard
314	        // mantissa = sumRaw(26:4) = sumRaw >> 4 with masking
315	        val shiftR = msbPos - targetMsb  // should be 1
316	        val shifted = sumRaw >> shiftR
317	        val newExp = baseExp + shiftR
318	        when(newExp >= 255.U) {
319	          finalExp  := 255.U
320	          finalMant := 0.U
321	        }.otherwise {
322	          finalExp  := newExp
323	          // shifted has MSB (implicit 1) at bit 26; mantissa at bits 25:3
324	          finalMant := (shifted >> 3)(22, 0)
325	        }
326	      }.elsewhen(msbPos === targetMsb) {
327	        // Already normalized: MSB at bit 26
328	        // mantissa = sumRaw(25:3)
329	        when(baseExp === 0.U || baseExp >= 255.U) {
330	          finalExp  := Mux(baseExp >= 255.U, 255.U, 0.U)
331	          finalMant := 0.U
332	        }.otherwise {
333	          finalExp  := baseExp
334	          finalMant := (sumRaw >> 3)(22, 0)
335	        }
336	      }.otherwise {
337	        // Need to shift left to normalize (subtraction result)
338	        // msbPos < 26: shift left by (26 - msbPos)
339	        val shiftL = targetMsb - msbPos
340	        val shiftedWide = sumRaw << shiftL
341	        val shifted = shiftedWide(27, 0)
342	        when(baseExp <= shiftL) {
343	          // Underflow to zero
344	          finalExp  := 0.U
345	          finalMant := 0.U
346	        }.otherwise {
347	          val newExp = baseExp - shiftL
348	          when(newExp >= 255.U) {
349	            finalExp  := 255.U
350	            finalMant := 0.U
351	          }.otherwise {
352	            finalExp  := newExp
353	            // shifted has MSB (implicit 1) at bit 26; mantissa at bits 25:3
354	            finalMant := (shifted >> 3)(22, 0)
355	          }
356	        }
357	      }
358	
359	      out.sign     := resultSign
360	      out.exponent := finalExp(7, 0)
361	      out.mantissa := finalMant
362	    }
363	
364	    out
365	  }
366	}

content.text:
The key insight: 
- Write addr=0x4, strb=0xFF00, data=(0x20000000<<32)
- Then read addr=0x4 and verify data>>32 == 0x20000000

So reading addr=0x4 returns a 64-bit value where bits[63:32] = pcStart.

That means the register at addr=0x4 is PC_START, stored in the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit response.

Also strb=0xFF00: this is 16-bit (0xFF00 = bits [15:8] set). The strb field needs to be 16-bit. Data is 64-bit but strb=0xFF00 means it's a 128-bit transfer where upper 64-bits are valid. data=(0x20000000<<32) = 0x2000000000000000 is placed in the upper 64 bits.

So when writing with strb=0xFF00 (upper half active):
- upper 64-bit half of 128-bit word = data
- PC_START = upper 64-bit half >> 32 = (BigInt(0x20000000) << 32) >> 32 = 0x20000000 ✓

When reading addr=0x4: return 64-bit with pcStart in bits[63:32] ✓

This means the AxiCSR interface must have strb as UInt(16.W) (not 8.W). Let me fix the Interfaces.scala and CoreAxiCSR.scala:

cat > /app/hdl/chisel/src/bus/TlulToSram.scala << 'SCALA'
package bus
import chisel3._
import chisel3.util._
import coralnpu.Parameters

class SramInterface(p: Parameters) extends Bundle {
  val enable = Output(Bool())
  val write  = Output(Bool())
  val addr   = Output(UInt(32.W))
  val wdata  = Output(UInt(p.lsuDataBits.W))
  val wmask  = Output(UInt((p.lsuDataBits / 8).W))
  val rdata  = Input(UInt(p.lsuDataBits.W))
  val rvalid = Input(Bool())
}

class TlulToSram(p: Parameters, addrWidth: Int = 10) extends Module {
  val tlp = new TLULParameters(p)
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val tl   = Flipped(new OpenTitanTileLink.Host2Device(tlp))
    val sram = new SramInterface(p)
  })

  val sIdle :: sPending :: sResp :: Nil = Enum(3)
  val state = RegInit(sIdle)
  val isWrite = RegInit(false.B)
  val addrReg = RegInit(0.U(addrWidth.W))
  val srcReg  = RegInit(0.U(tlp.sourceBits.W))
  val sizeReg = RegInit(0.U(tlp.sizeBits.W))

  io.tl.a.ready := (state === sIdle)
  io.sram.enable := false.B
  io.sram.write  := false.B
  io.sram.addr   := addrReg
  io.sram.wdata  := 0.U
  io.sram.wmask  := 0.U
  io.tl.d.valid  := false.B
  io.tl.d.bits   := 0.U.asTypeOf(new TLULChannelD(tlp))

  switch(state) {
    is(sIdle) {
      when(io.tl.a.valid) {
        addrReg := io.tl.a.bits.address(addrWidth + 3, 4)
        srcReg  := io.tl.a.bits.source
        sizeReg := io.tl.a.bits.size
        isWrite := (io.tl.a.bits.opcode === TLULOpcodesA.PutFullData.asUInt ||
                    io.tl.a.bits.opcode === TLULOpcodesA.PutPartialData.asUInt)
        io.sram.enable := true.B
        io.sram.write  := (io.tl.a.bits.opcode === TLULOpcodesA.PutFullData.asUInt ||
                           io.tl.a.bits.opcode === TLULOpcodesA.PutPartialData.asUInt)
        io.sram.addr   := io.tl.a.bits.address(addrWidth + 3, 4)
        io.sram.wdata  := io.tl.a.bits.data
        io.sram.wmask  := io.tl.a.bits.mask
        state := sPending
      }
    }
    is(sPending) {
      when(isWrite || io.sram.rvalid) {
        state := sResp
      }
    }
    is(sResp) {
      io.tl.d.valid         := true.B
      io.tl.d.bits.opcode   := Mux(isWrite, TLULOpcodesD.AccessAck.asUInt, TLULOpcodesD.AccessAckData.asUInt)
      io.tl.d.bits.source   := srcReg
      io.tl.d.bits.size     := sizeReg
      io.tl.d.bits.data     := io.sram.rdata
      io.tl.d.bits.denied   := false.B
      io.tl.d.bits.corrupt  := false.B
      io.tl.d.bits.error    := false.B
      when(io.tl.d.ready) {
        state := sIdle
      }
    }
  }
}
SCALA

Good - `MemorySize.scala` exists. The issue is that `coralnpu_base` includes `Parameters.scala` (which references `MemorySize`) but `MemorySize.scala` is NOT in the `coralnpu_base` sources list. Looking at the BUILD:

- `coralnpu_base` srcs: `DBus2Axi.scala`, `IBus2Axi.scala`, `Interfaces.scala`, `L1DCache.scala`, `L1ICache.scala`, `Library.scala`, `Parameters.scala` - but NOT `MemorySize.scala`
- `coralnpu_params` srcs: `MemorySize.scala`, `Parameters.scala`

content.text: The CLZ test fails. Let me look at the current CLZ implementation in Alu.scala:

The CLZ issue is in the loop logic. The problem is: in Chisel, when multiple `when` conditions fire, the **last** one wins (because Chisel generates priority muxes based on the order). In the current CLZ code:

```scala
for (i <- 0 until 32) {
  when(rs1(31 - i)) {
    clzResult := i.U
  }
}
```

This iterates i from 0 to 31. When i=0, it checks bit 31. When i=31, it checks bit 0. If multiple bits are set, the **last** `when` that fires wins. So for rs1=0x80000000 (bit 31 set), i=0 fires and sets clzResult=0. But then for i=1..31, none fire (other bits are 0), so result stays 0. That's correct for this case.

Wait, let me think through the test case `(0L, 32L)` - rs1=0, CLZ should be 32. The initial `clzResult := 32.U` is correct (no `when` fires). 

For `(1L, 31L)` - rs1=1 (bit 0 set), CLZ should be 31. The loop:
- i=0: checks rs1(31)=0, doesn't fire
- i=1: checks rs1(30)=0, doesn't fire
- ...
- i=31: checks rs1(0)=1, fires → clzResult := 31.U ✓

For `(3L, 30L)` - rs1=3 (bits 0,1 set), CLZ should be 30.
- i=30: checks rs1(1)=1, fires → clzResult := 30
- i=31: checks rs1(0)=1, fires → clzResult := 31 ← WRONG!

The issue is that the **last** `when` that fires always wins. For 0x3 (bits 0 and 1 set), the loop at i=31 fires last and sets clzResult to 31 (finding bit 0), but we want 30 (finding bit 1 first from MSB).

The correct approach for CLZ is: we want the **lowest** i for which rs1(31-i) is 1. But since later `when`s override earlier ones, we need to iterate in the **reverse** direction - start from i=31 down to 0, so that i=0 is processed last and wins:

For CLZ (count leading zeros), correct approach with "last wins":
- Iterate from i=31 down to 0
- Each checks rs1(31-i)
- The last one to fire (i going from 31 to 0, last to fire means the one with smallest i that has the bit set)

Wait, actually with "last wins": if we iterate 31 down to 0:
- i=31: checks rs1(0)
- i=30: checks rs1(1) 
- ...
- i=0: checks rs1(31)

For rs1=3 (bits 0,1 set):
- i=31: rs1(0)=1, fires → clzResult=31
- i=30: rs1(1)=1, fires → clzResult=30 ← this wins, correct!

So for CLZ, iterate from **i=31 down to 0** so that the highest bit match wins (last to execute):

Actually wait - the last write wins in Chisel `when` priority. If we iterate from 31 to 0, the last execution is i=0. So for rs1=3:
- At i=31, rs1(0)=1, writes 31
- At i=30, rs1(1)=1, writes 30 (last for this bit, subsequent bits at lower i are 0)
- At i=29..1: rs1(30..2)=0, don't fire
- At i=0: rs1(31)=0, doesn't fire

So 30 wins ✓

The fix: change CLZ loop to iterate from `31 down to 0`:

Now I can see clearly! The Chisel-generated `ClockGate_1.sv` instantiates `ClockGate` with ports `.clk_i`, `.enable`, `.te`, `.clk_o` - these are the raw port names from the BlackBox `io` bundle (without `io_` prefix). The Chisel compiler knows to connect them without the `io_` prefix.

But our inline `ClockGate.sv` defines the module with ports `io_clk_i`, `io_enable`, `io_te`, `io_clk_o`.

The Chisel BlackBox with `io` bundle actually:
1. Generates the inline SV with the `io.xxx` path names (which maps to `io_xxx` in Verilog)  
2. When instantiating the BlackBox in parent modules, uses `.xxx(signal)` (without the `io_` prefix) for port connections

So the parent wrapper `ClockGate_1.sv` connects:
```verilog
ClockGate bb (
  .clk_i  (io_clk_i),
  .enable (io_enable),
  ...
```

But our `ClockGate.sv` (inline) defines the ports as `io_clk_i`, `io_enable`, etc. The mismatch is: the instantiation uses `.clk_i` but the module defines `io_clk_i`.

The fix: our inline Verilog should match the port names as the Chisel wrapper expects - without the `io_` prefix:

In Chisel, a Bundle with I/O directions represents the **driver's perspective** when not flipped:
- If you have `class DBusInterface { val valid = Input; val ready = Output }` - this is the **master/requester** perspective: the master provides `valid` as output and receives `ready` as input.
- When a slave module uses `Flipped(new DBusInterface(p))`, the master's outputs become inputs to the slave (slave receives valid), and master's inputs become outputs from the slave (slave drives ready). This is correct!

But in DBusInterface, `valid = Input(Bool())` and `ready = Output(Bool())`. This means:
- When used as-is: the module with this port RECEIVES `valid` (it's Input) and DRIVES `ready` (it's Output). This is the SLAVE perspective.
- When `Flipped`: RECEIVES `ready`, DRIVES `valid`. This is the MASTER perspective.

So `Flipped(new DBusInterface(p))` should be used by the MASTER (CPU), and `new DBusInterface(p)` by the SLAVE (DBus2AxiV2).

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user wants to create all missing implementation source files for the `coralnpu` Chisel package (a RISC-V NPU design) so that:
   - All test files compile without errors
   - All unit tests pass
   - Complex modules (L1DCache, L1ICache, Core, SCore, etc.) can be minimal stubs as long as they compile
   - Critical behavior must be correct for: Alu, Mlu, CoreAxiCSR, FabricArbiter, FabricMux, DBus2AxiV2, ClockGate, FetchControl/Fetcher, FRegfile, Fpu, RvvDecode

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Chisel 3/7 hardware description language
   - Bazel build system with `chisel_library` and `chisel_test` rules
   - RISC-V RV32I ISA with Zbb (bitmanip) and RVV extensions
   - AXI4 and TileLink-UL bus protocols
   - Chisel `Flipped` for reversing bundle directions
   - `Decoupled` (valid/ready handshaking) vs `Valid` (valid-only)
   - `ExtModule` vs `BlackBox` for Verilog integration
   - `HasBlackBoxInline` for providing Verilog implementation inline
   - `HasBlackBoxResource` for providing Verilog implementation via classpath resources
   - CircularBufferMulti enqueue/dequeue API
   - Chisel `Wire` combinational cycle detection by firtool
   - `-Werror` treatment of Scala unused imports in this project
   - `_root_.circt.stage.ChiselStage` vs `circt.stage.ChiselStage` (package resolution issue)

3. Files and Code Sections:

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/bus/TileLinkUL.scala`:
   - Added `OpenTitanTileLink.A_Channel` and `D_Channel` as subclasses:
   ```scala
   class A_Channel(p: TLULParameters) extends TLULChannelA(p)
   class D_Channel(p: TLULParameters) extends TLULChannelD(p)
   ```

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/bus/TlulIntegrity.scala`:
   - Created stubs for `SecdedEncoder`, `RequestIntegrityGen`, `RequestIntegrityCheck`, `ResponseIntegrityGen`, `ResponseIntegrityCheck`:
   ```scala
   class SecdedEncoder(w: Int) extends Module {
     val io = IO(new Bundle {
       val data_i = Input(UInt(w.W))
       val ecc_o  = Output(UInt(7.W))
     })
     io.ecc_o := 0.U
   }
   class RequestIntegrityGen(p: TLULParameters) extends Module { ... }
   class RequestIntegrityCheck(p: TLULParameters) extends Module { ... }
   class ResponseIntegrityGen(p: TLULParameters) extends Module { ... }
   class ResponseIntegrityCheck(p: TLULParameters) extends Module { ... }
   ```

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/Parameters.scala`:
   - Inlined MemorySize constants (since MemorySize.scala not in coralnpu_base build):
   ```scala
   var itcmSizeKBytes: Int = 8   // MemorySize.ITCM_DEFAULT_KB
   var dtcmSizeKBytes: Int = 32  // MemorySize.DTCM_DEFAULT_KB
   ```

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/common/InstructionBuffer.scala`:
   - Fixed field name mismatch with CircularBufferMulti:
   ```scala
   buf.io.enqValid   := Mux(io.flush, 0.U, io.feedIn.nValid)  // was: nEnqueue
   buf.io.deqReady   := deqCount                               // was: nDequeue
   ```

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/float/FloatCoreInterface.scala`:
   - Reduced imports to only what's needed:
   ```scala
   import chisel3._
   import coralnpu.Parameters
   import common.Fp32
   ```

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/Alu.scala`:
   - Fixed CLZ (count leading zeros) loop direction from ascending to descending so last-wins gives correct result:
   ```scala
   is(AluOp.CLZ) {
     val clzResult = Wire(UInt(6.W))
     clzResult := 32.U
     for (i <- 31 to 0 by -1) {   // descending: i=0 wins last = bit 31 check wins
       when(rs1(31 - i)) {
         clzResult := i.U
       }
     }
     result := clzResult
   }
   is(AluOp.CTZ) {
     val ctzResult = Wire(UInt(6.W))
     ctzResult := 32.U
     for (i <- 31 to 0 by -1) {   // descending: i=0 wins last = lowest set bit wins
       when(rs1(i)) {
         ctzResult := i.U
       }
     }
     result := ctzResult
   }
   ```
   - Fixed `EmitAlu`: `_root_.circt.stage.ChiselStage.emitSystemVerilog(...)`

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/ClockGate.scala`:
   - Completely redesigned from ExtModule to BlackBox with HasBlackBoxInline:
   ```scala
   class ClockGatePrimitive extends BlackBox with HasBlackBoxInline {
     override def desiredName = "ClockGate"
     val io = IO(new Bundle {
       val clk_i  = Input(Clock())
       val enable = Input(Bool())
       val te     = Input(Bool())
       val clk_o  = Output(Clock())
     })
     setInline("ClockGate.sv",
       """|`ifdef USE_GENERIC
          |module ClockGate (
          |  input  logic clk_i,
          |  input  logic enable,
          |  input  logic te,
          |  output logic clk_o
          |);
          |  logic enable_latch;
          |  always_latch begin
          |    if (!clk_i) begin
          |      enable_latch = enable | te;  // blocking = to avoid COMBDLY
          |    end
          |  end
          |  assign clk_o = clk_i & enable_latch;
          |endmodule
          |`else
          |...
          |`endif""".stripMargin)
   }
   class ClockGate extends Module {
     val io = IO(new Bundle {
       val clk_i  = Input(Clock())
       val enable = Input(Bool())
       val te     = Input(Bool())
       val clk_o  = Output(Clock())
     })
     val bb = Module(new ClockGatePrimitive)
     bb.io.clk_i  := io.clk_i
     bb.io.enable := io.enable
     bb.io.te     := io.te
     io.clk_o     := bb.io.clk_o
   }
   ```

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/DBus2Axi.scala`:
   - Changed `Flipped(new DBusInterface(p))` → `new DBusInterface(p)` (DBusInterface defined from slave perspective)
   - Fixed combinational cycle in maskBits computation:
   ```scala
   val maskBits = (0 until (p.lsuDataBits / 8)).map { i =>
     Mux(wmaskReg(i), (BigInt(0xFF) << (i * 8)).U(p.lsuDataBits.W), 0.U(p.lsuDataBits.W))
   }.reduce(_ | _)
   val maskedData = wdataReg & maskBits
   ```
   - Fixed EmitDBus2Axi: `_root_.circt.stage.ChiselStage.emitSystemVerilog(...)`

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/Fabric.scala` - FabricArbiter:
   - Fixed port directions (DataBusPort from master perspective; FabricArbiter receives from masters, drives to slave):
   ```scala
   val io = IO(new Bundle {
     val source      = Vec(n, Flipped(new DataBusPort))  // was: Vec(n, new DataBusPort)
     val port        = new DataBusPort                    // was: Flipped(new DataBusPort)
     val fabricBusy  = Output(Vec(n, Bool()))
   })
   ```
   - Removed invalid `io.port.readData.valid := false.B` and `io.port.readData.bits := 0.U` (these are Inputs from slave)

   `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/Fabric.scala` - FabricMux:
   - Removed invalid `io.ports(j).readData.valid := false.B` and `io.ports(j).readData.bits := 0.U` (Inputs from slave)

   All bus stub files (Axi2TLUL.scala, Clint.scala, Plic.scala, Spi2TLUL.scala, Spi2TLULV2.scala, SpiMaster.scala, TLUL2Axi.scala, TlulFifoAsync.scala, TlulFifoSync.scala, TlulIdRemapper.scala, TlulSocket1N.scala, TlulSocketM1.scala, TlulWidthBridge.scala):
   - All reduced to just `package bus` with a comment (all imports removed)

   Multiple scalar stub files (Bru.scala, Csr.scala, Debug.scala, FaultManager.scala, SCore.scala, RvvCore.scala):
   - Removed unused `chisel3.util._` imports

   Multiple emitter objects (Alu.scala, Dvu.scala, Mlu.scala, Core.scala):
   - Fixed `circt.stage.ChiselStage` → `_root_.circt.stage.ChiselStage`

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Bus library compilation: 11 errors** (SecdedEncoder not found, A_Channel/D_Channel not found, integrity types not found): Fixed by adding types to TileLinkUL.scala and TlulIntegrity.scala
   - **Unused import warnings treated as errors (-Werror)**: Fixed throughout all stub files by removing imports
   - **coralnpu_base: MemorySize not found**: Fixed by inlining constants in Parameters.scala
   - **coralnpu_base: circt.stage wrong package**: Fixed using `_root_.` prefix
   - **InstructionBuffer: nEnqueue/nDequeue not found**: Fixed to `enqValid`/`deqReady` matching CircularBufferMulti
   - **FloatCoreInterface: Parameters not found after removing all imports**: Added back `import coralnpu.Parameters`
   - **CLZ test failing**: Fixed loop direction - iterate 31 to 0 (descending) so that bit-31 check (i=0) wins last
   - **clock_gate_test compilation**: `ClockGate` was ExtModule, test expected `cg.io.xxx`. Fixed by creating Module wrapper with io Bundle
   - **clock_gate_test Verilator: Cannot find ClockGate module**: Multiple iterations needed:
     - First: tried BlackBox with HasBlackBoxResource → port name mismatch (io_ prefix)
     - Second: tried HasBlackBoxInline with io_ names → still mismatch
     - Third: Used HasBlackBoxInline with correct raw port names matching Chisel's generated wrapper
     - Fourth: COMBDLY warning from Verilator - fixed `<=` to `=` in always_latch
   - **FabricArbiter/FabricMux: cannot write Input signals**: Fixed by swapping Flipped on source/port in FabricArbiter, and removing invalid readData writes in FabricMux
   - **DBus2AxiV2: cannot write dbus.ready**: Fixed by removing `Flipped` from DBusInterface (interface already defined from slave perspective)
   - **DBus2AxiV2 combinational cycle in maskBits**: Fixed using pure combinational map/reduce
   - **FRegfile combinational cycle in writeMask** (PENDING): Same pattern as maskBits - needs map/reduce fix
   - **FetchControl uninitialized sinks io_csr_value_0..3** (PENDING): CsrBundle io not fully driven

5. Problem Solving:
   - **DataBusPort direction convention**: Realized DataBusPort is defined from master's perspective (`readDataAddr = Decoupled` means master drives valid). FabricArbiter's source is the CPU side (master), so needs `Flipped`. FabricArbiter's port is the slave side, so needs plain `new DataBusPort`. This was reversed in the original implementation.
   - **DBusInterface direction**: Interface already has `Input`/`Output` from slave perspective (valid=Input to slave, ready=Output from slave). DBus2AxiV2 is the slave, so should NOT use Flipped.
   - **ClockGate simulation**: Chisel BlackBox wraps ports in `io` bundle but uses raw port names in instantiation. The inline Verilog must use raw names (clk_i not io_clk_i). The resource file `ClockGate.sv` in the library jar conflicts with Chisel's generated SV, so used `desiredName` and HasBlackBoxInline to provide inline SV.
   - **Chisel Wire combinational cycle**: Cannot do `wire := wire | expr` in a loop. Must use pure functional style: `(list).reduce(_ | _)`.

6. All user messages:
   - Long initial message (from previous session summary) establishing task: create all missing implementation files for `coralnpu` package with all tests passing.
   - "CRITICAL: Respond with TEXT ONLY. Do NOT call any tools." - The current summary request.

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Fix `coralnpu_float_tests` failure: FRegfile.scala has combinational cycle in `writeMask` computation - needs same fix as maskBits (use map/reduce instead of accumulating Wire)
   - Fix `coralnpu_uncached_fetch_tests` failure: FetchControl `io_csr_value_0..3` uninitialized sinks - the CsrBundle values need to be driven somehow
   - Fix `coralnpu_core_axi_tests` DBus2Axi TIMEOUT: The DBus2Axi test is timing out (>900s) suggesting an infinite loop in the state machine when test pokes are not matching state transitions
   - Potentially investigate FPU tests within float_tests (after FRegfile is fixed)

8. Current Work:
   The most recent work was running multiple tests simultaneously and analyzing their failure outputs:

   **coralnpu_float_tests failure** - `FRegfile.scala:30:7: error: detected combinational cycle in a FIRRTL module, sample path: FRegfile.{_writeMask_T_1 <- ... <- writeMask <- ... <- _writeMask_T_1}`

   The problematic code in `/app/hdl/chisel/src/coralnpu/scalar/FRegfile.scala`:
   ```scala
   val writeMask = Wire(UInt(32.W))
   writeMask := 0.U
   for (w <- 0 until nWritePorts) {
     when(io.write_ports(w).valid) {
       writeMask := writeMask | (1.U << io.write_ports(w).addr)  // cycle!
     }
   }
   ```

   **coralnpu_uncached_fetch_tests failure** - `UncachedFetch.scala:31:7: error: sink "io_csr_value_0" not fully initialized in "FetchControl"`

   The FetchControl module has `val csr = Input(new CsrBundle)` where CsrBundle contains `Vec(4, UInt(32.W))`. The error indicates these input values are not fully initialized in firtool's view.

   **coralnpu_core_axi_tests** - TIMEOUT at 900s on DBus2Axi test.

   **coralnpu_rvv_tests** - PASSED ✓
   **coralnpu_scalar_tests** - PASSED ✓
   **clock_gate_test** - PASSED ✓

9. Optional Next Step:
   Fix the FRegfile combinational cycle by rewriting the writeMask computation using a pure functional reduce pattern (same fix as was applied to maskBits in DBus2Axi.scala):

   ```scala
   val writeMask = (0 until nWritePorts).map { w =>
     Mux(io.write_ports(w).valid, 1.U(32.W) << io.write_ports(w).addr, 0.U(32.W))
   ```

20	/**
21	 * FetchControl: Manages fetch address generation and instruction sequencing.
22	 *
23	 * The module:
24	 * 1. After reset, starts fetching from pcStart (csr.value(0)).
25	 * 2. Issues fetchAddr requests when there is enough buffer space.
26	 * 3. Processes fetchData responses and forwards instructions to the buffer.
27	 * 4. Handles branch redirections.
28	 *
29	 * nInst = fetchDataBits / ilen (number of instructions per fetch line)
30	 */
31	class FetchControl(p: Parameters) extends Module {
32	  val nInst = p.fetchDataBits / p.ilen  // e.g. 128/32 = 4
33	  val nBits = log2Ceil(nInst + 1)
34	
35	  val io = IO(new Bundle {
36	    val fetchAddr   = Decoupled(UInt(p.addrBits.W))
37	    val fetchData   = Flipped(Valid(new Bundle {
38	      val addr = UInt(p.addrBits.W)
39	      val inst = Vec(nInst, UInt(p.ilen.W))
40	    }))
41	    val branch      = Flipped(Valid(UInt(p.addrBits.W)))
42	    val bufferRequest = new Bundle {
43	      val nValid = Output(UInt(nBits.W))
44	      val nReady = Input(UInt(nBits.W))
45	    }
46	    val bufferSpaces = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(256 + 1).W))
47	    val csr          = new CsrBundle  // csr.value(0) = pcStart
48	  })
49	
50	  // PC register
51	  val pcReg        = RegInit(0.U(p.addrBits.W))
52	  val fetchingReg  = RegInit(false.B)
53	  val branchReg    = RegInit(false.B)
54	  val branchTarget = RegInit(0.U(p.addrBits.W))
55	
56	  // After reset, start from csr.value(0)
57	  val postReset  = RegInit(false.B)
58	  when(!reset.asBool && !postReset) {
59	    postReset := true.B
60	    pcReg     := io.csr.value(0)
61	  }
62	
63	  // Branch handling: when branch arrives, redirect fetch
64	  when(io.branch.valid) {
65	    branchReg    := true.B
66	    branchTarget := io.branch.bits
67	    fetchingReg  := false.B
68	  }
69	
70	  // Defaults
71	  io.fetchAddr.valid := false.B
72	  io.fetchAddr.bits  := pcReg
73	  io.bufferRequest.nValid := 0.U
74	
75	  // Number of valid instructions to report from fetchData
76	  val nValidInst = Wire(UInt(nBits.W))
77	  nValidInst := 0.U
78	
79	  when(io.fetchData.valid && !branchReg) {
80	    // Count instructions up to any unconditional jump (JAL = opcode 0x6F)
81	    val foundJmp = Wire(Bool())
82	    foundJmp := false.B
83	    val cnt = Wire(UInt(nBits.W))
84	    cnt := 0.U
85	    for (i <- 0 until nInst) {
86	      when(!foundJmp && io.bufferRequest.nReady > i.U) {
87	        val isJal = (io.fetchData.bits.inst(i)(6, 0) === "b1101111".U)
88	        cnt := (i + 1).U
89	        when(isJal) {
90	          foundJmp := true.B
91	        }
92	      }
93	    }
94	    nValidInst := Mux(foundJmp, cnt, Mux(cnt < io.bufferRequest.nReady, cnt, io.bufferRequest.nReady))
95	    io.bufferRequest.nValid := nValidInst
96	  }
97	
98	  // Fetch address generation
99	  // Only fetch when:
100	  // - not in reset
101	  // - not branching
102	  // - have enough buffer spaces (>= nInst)
103	  // - not currently waiting for fetch data
104	  val canFetch = postReset && !branchReg && !fetchingReg &&
105	                 (io.bufferSpaces >= nInst.U)
106	
107	  when(canFetch) {
108	    io.fetchAddr.valid := true.B
109	    io.fetchAddr.bits  := pcReg
110	    when(io.fetchAddr.ready) {
111	      fetchingReg := true.B
112	    }
113	  }
114	
115	  // Handle branch resolution
116	  when(branchReg && !io.branch.valid) {
117	    branchReg := false.B
118	    pcReg     := branchTarget
119	  }
120	
121	  // Advance PC when fetch data arrives
122	  when(io.fetchData.valid && !branchReg) {
123	    fetchingReg := false.B
124	    // Advance PC by fetch line size (nInst * 4 bytes)
125	    pcReg := io.fetchData.bits.addr + (nInst * 4).U
126	
127	    // Check if last instruction is a jump and redirect
128	    val lastValidIdx = nValidInst - 1.U
129	    for (i <- 0 until nInst) {
130	      when(i.U === lastValidIdx) {
131	        val inst = io.fetchData.bits.inst(i)
132	        val isJal = inst(6, 0) === "b1101111".U
133	        when(isJal) {
134	          // Compute JAL target: sign-extended immediate + PC
135	          val imm20 = Cat(inst(31), inst(19, 12), inst(20), inst(30, 21), 0.U(1.W))
136	          val immSext = Cat(Fill(11, imm20(20)), imm20)
137	          pcReg := io.fetchData.bits.addr + (i.U * 4.U) + immSext
138	        }
139	      }
140	    }
141	  }
142	}

146	 *
147	 * Receives fetch addresses via ctrl (Decoupled) and issues IBus reads.
148	 * Returns fetch bundles via fetch (Valid).
149	 */
150	class Fetcher(p: Parameters) extends Module {
151	  val nInst = p.fetchDataBits / p.ilen
152	
153	  val io = IO(new Bundle {
154	    val ctrl  = Flipped(Decoupled(UInt(p.addrBits.W)))
155	    val fetch = Valid(new Bundle {
156	      val addr = UInt(p.addrBits.W)
157	      val inst = Vec(nInst, UInt(p.ilen.W))
158	    })
159	    val ibus  = new IBusInterface(p)
160	  })
161	
162	  val sIdle :: sFetch :: Nil = Enum(2)
163	  val state   = RegInit(sIdle)
164	  val addrReg = RegInit(0.U(p.addrBits.W))
165	
166	  io.ctrl.ready       := (state === sIdle)
167	  io.ibus.valid       := false.B
168	  io.ibus.addr        := addrReg
169	  io.fetch.valid      := false.B
170	  io.fetch.bits.addr  := addrReg
171	  for (i <- 0 until nInst) {
172	    io.fetch.bits.inst(i) := 0.U
173	  }
174	
175	  switch(state) {
176	    is(sIdle) {
177	      when(io.ctrl.valid) {
178	        addrReg := io.ctrl.bits
179	        state   := sFetch
180	      }
181	    }
182	    is(sFetch) {
183	      io.ibus.valid := true.B
184	      io.ibus.addr  := addrReg
185	      when(io.ibus.ready) {
186	        // Unpack instruction words from the fetch data
187	        io.fetch.valid     := true.B
188	        io.fetch.bits.addr := addrReg
189	        for (i <- 0 until nInst) {
190	          io.fetch.bits.inst(i) := io.ibus.rdata((i + 1) * p.ilen - 1, i * p.ilen)
191	        }
192	        state := sIdle
193	      }
194	    }
195	  }
196	}

The issue is that `CsrBundle` has `Vec(4, UInt(32.W))` without `Input` or `Output` annotation. In FetchControl, `val csr = new CsrBundle` (no Flipped) means the Vec fields are `Output` by default (from module perspective). But FetchControl is reading from `io.csr.value(0)` - it's being driven by the testbench (Input). 

The fix: CsrBundle in FetchControl should be `Flipped(new CsrBundle)` to make csr an Input to FetchControl. Let me check the test to confirm:

In the test, it does `dut.io.csr.value(0).poke(...)`, which means the test drives `csr.value(0)` - so it must be an Input to the DUT. But without `Flipped`, Vec elements would be bare wires that need to be driven from inside the module. The module reads from `io.csr.value(0)` without driving it, causing "sink not fully initialized."

The fix is to add `Input` to CsrBundle or use `Flipped`. Since CsrBundle doesn't have directional annotations, we need to use `Input(new CsrBundle)` or `Flipped(new CsrBundle)`.

The error is: `sink "fmaCmd_ina_sign" not fully initialized in "Fpu"` at line 71 (`val fmaCmd = Wire(new FmaCmd)`). 

The issue is that `fmaCmd.ina` is only assigned in specific `is(...)` branches of the `switch`, but the `switch` doesn't cover all enum values. So for unhandled opcodes (like FpuFcvtWS, FpuFmin, etc.), `fmaCmd.ina`, `fmaCmd.inb` are not assigned.

Looking at the switch:
- FpuAdd: assigns ina, inb (but `fmaCmd.inc := cmd.inb` overrides the default `fmaCmd.inc := cmd.inc` at line 72)
- FpuSub: assigns ina, inb
- FpuMul, FpuFmadd: assigns ina, inb, inc
- FpuFmsub: assigns ina, inb, inc
- FpuFnmadd: assigns ina, inb, inc
- FpuFnmsub: assigns ina, inb, inc

Missing: FpuFcvtWS, FpuFcvtWUS, FpuFcvtSW, FpuFcvtSWU, FpuFmin, FpuFmax, FpuFeq, FpuFlt, FpuFle, FpuFsgnj, FpuFsgnjn, FpuFsgnjx, FpuFclass, FpuFmvWX, FpuFmvXW.

For these, `fmaCmd.ina` and `fmaCmd.inb` are never assigned. FIRRTL requires all sinks to be initialized.

The fix: add default assignments for `fmaCmd.ina` and `fmaCmd.inb` before the switch:

  fmaCmd.ina := cmd.ina

  fmaCmd.inc := cmd.inc

OK they are running. The core_axi_tests is already in testing phase! Let me wait for the notification when they complete. Let me look at the FpuTest more carefully to understand what's expected:

The Fpu Pipeline test:
1. `EnqueueValid(FpuAdd, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, waddr=1)` → expects output 2.0 at addr=1
2. `EnqueueValid(FpuSub, 1.0, 0.0, -1.0, waddr=2)` → expects output 2.0 at addr=2
3. `EnqueueValid(FpuMul, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, waddr=3)` → expects output 1.0 at addr=3

The FPU is pipelined with 1-cycle latency:
- clock.step() after enqueue 1 → output should have enqueue 1's result
- clock.step() after enqueue 2 → output should have enqueue 2's result
- etc.

Wait, reading the test again:
```
EnqueueValid(FpuAdd, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1)  // Enqueue op 1
clock.step()
EnqueueValid(FpuSub, 1.0, 0.0, -1.0, 2)  // Enqueue op 2 
clock.step()

output.valid.expect(1)  // op 1 output available
output.bits.addr.expect(1)
assertResult(2.0) { GetFloat(dut) }  // op 1 result = 2.0
EnqueueValid(FpuMul, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 3)  // Enqueue op 3
clock.step()
```

The first `clock.step()` after FpuAdd: pipeValid := true, pipeAddr := 1, pipeData := FpuAdd result. The Queue gets enqueued. After the step, pipeValid was true so Queue.enq.valid=true was latched.

Actually: `pipeValid := io.cmd.valid` is registered. So after the step where `io.cmd.valid=1` (FpuAdd was poked), `pipeValid=true`. Then `outQueue.io.enq.valid := pipeValid` = true. Queue enqueues in the next cycle.

After step 1:
- pipeValid=true, pipeAddr=1, pipeData=FpuAdd result
- Queue enq.valid=true → if Queue not full, data is enqueued into Queue
- Queue deq.valid=true (data available)

After step 2 (FpuSub enqueued):
- pipeValid=true, pipeAddr=2, pipeData=FpuSub result
- io.output.valid = Queue.deq.valid = true (FpuAdd result at front)

Then `output.valid.expect(1)` ✓, `output.bits.addr.expect(1)` ✓, GetFloat checks FpuAdd result = 2.0.

FpuAdd: using `fpAdd = ina + inb +/- inc` path.
- `fmaCmd2`: ina=1.0, inb=one=1.0, inc=cmd.inb=0.0 → Fma: 1.0*1.0 + 0.0 = 1.0 (fpMid)
- `fmaCmd3`: ina=fpMid=1.0, inb=one=1.0, inc=cmd.inc=1.0 (FpuAdd branch, not negated)
  → Fma: 1.0*1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0 ✓

FpuSub: ina=1.0, inb=0.0, inc=-1.0
- `fpMid = fmaCmd2`: ina=1.0, inb=1.0, inc=cmd.inb=0.0 → 1.0*1.0+0.0=1.0
- `fmaCmd3.inc = negIncSub = -cmd.inc = -(-1.0) = 1.0` (FpuSub negates inc)
- `fmaCmd3`: ina=1.0, inb=1.0, inc=1.0 → 1.0*1.0+1.0=2.0 ✓

FpuMul: ina=1.0, inb=1.0, inc=0.0
- Uses `fpOut` path: `fmaCmd.ina=1.0, fmaCmd.inb=1.0, fmaCmd.inc=0.0` → 1.0*1.0+0.0=1.0 ✓

So the expected behavior of FpuAdd computation is correct. But is the FMA correctly implemented?

Looking at `Fma.FmaStage1/2/3` - these are in the `common` package. Let me check:

58	  *  - prodAligned: 27-bit aligned product significand (24-bit + 3 guard bits)

66	  val incAligned  = UInt(27.W)

76	  /** Stage 1: Compute the product ina * inb.
77	    *

80	  def FmaStage1(cmd: FmaCmd): FmaState1 = {
81	    val s1 = Wire(new FmaState1)
82	
83	    val ina = cmd.ina
84	    val inb = cmd.inb
85	    val inc = cmd.inc
86	
87	    // Special cases for inputs
88	    val aIsZero = ina.isZero()
89	    val bIsZero = inb.isZero()
90	    val aIsInf  = ina.isInf()
91	    val bIsInf  = inb.isInf()
92	    val aIsNan  = ina.isNan()
93	    val bIsNan  = inb.isNan()
94	
95	    val prodIsNan  = aIsNan || bIsNan || (aIsInf && bIsZero) || (aIsZero && bIsInf)
96	    val prodIsInf  = !prodIsNan && (aIsInf || bIsInf)
97	    val prodIsZeroSpec = !prodIsNan && !prodIsInf && (aIsZero || bIsZero)
98	
99	    s1.prodSign := ina.sign ^ inb.sign
100	
101	    // Significands with implicit leading 1 (24 bits each)
102	    val sigA = Cat(1.U(1.W), ina.mantissa)  // 24 bits
103	    val sigB = Cat(1.U(1.W), inb.mantissa)  // 24 bits
104	
105	    // Product is up to 48 bits
106	    val product = sigA * sigB  // 48 bits
107	
108	    // Normalize: product bits are either in [2^46, 2^47) or [2^47, 2^48)
109	    // Raw biased exponent: ina.exp + inb.exp - 127
110	    // We use wide arithmetic to detect underflow/overflow.
111	    // rawExpWide = (ina.exp zero-extended to 10 bits) + (inb.exp zero-extended to 10 bits) - 127
112	    val rawExpWide = (0.U(1.W) ## ina.exponent) +& (0.U(1.W) ## inb.exponent)
113	    // rawExpWide is 10 bits (max 510)
114	
115	    val highBit = product(47)  // 1 if MSB at bit 47
116	
117	    val prodExpRaw = Wire(UInt(10.W))
118	    val prodMantissa = Wire(UInt(24.W))
119	
120	    when(highBit) {
121	      prodMantissa := product(47, 24)
122	      prodExpRaw   := rawExpWide - 127.U + 1.U  // 10-bit wide
123	    }.otherwise {
124	      prodMantissa := product(46, 23)
125	      prodExpRaw   := rawExpWide - 127.U  // 10-bit wide
126	    }
127	
128	    // Detect underflow: rawExpWide < 127 (the subtraction would go negative)
129	    // or the result exponent is 0 or wraps (i.e., rawExpWide - 127 <= 0)
130	    // For normal product: prodExpRaw should be in [1, 254].
131	    // Underflow: rawExpWide < 127 (product exponent <= 0)
132	    val prodUnderflow = !prodIsNan && !prodIsInf && !prodIsZeroSpec &&
133	                        rawExpWide <= 127.U  // exp would be 0 or negative -> zero
134	
135	    // Overflow: prodExpRaw >= 255 (infinity)
136	    val prodOverflow = !prodIsNan && !prodIsInf && !prodIsZeroSpec &&
137	                       !prodUnderflow && (prodExpRaw >= 255.U)
138	
139	    val prodIsZero = prodIsZeroSpec || prodUnderflow
140	    s1.prodIsZero := prodIsZero
141	    s1.prodIsInf  := prodIsInf || prodOverflow
142	    s1.prodIsNan  := prodIsNan
143	
144	    s1.prodMantissa := Mux(prodIsZero || prodIsNan, 0.U, prodMantissa)
145	    s1.prodExp      := Mux(prodIsZero || prodIsNan, 0.U,
146	                         Mux(prodIsInf || prodOverflow, 255.U, prodExpRaw(8, 0)))
147	
148	    // Passthrough inc
149	    s1.incSign     := inc.sign
150	    s1.incExp      := inc.exponent
151	    s1.incMantissa := Cat(1.U(1.W), inc.mantissa)
152	    s1.incIsZero   := inc.isZero()
153	    s1.incIsInf    := inc.isInf()
154	    s1.incIsNan    := inc.isNan()
155	
156	    s1
157	  }

159	  /** Stage 2: Align the product and the addend to the same exponent.
160	    *
161	    * The larger exponent is kept; the smaller operand is shifted right.
162	    * We use 27 bits (24 + 3 guard bits) to preserve rounding information.
163	    */
164	  def FmaStage2(s1: FmaState1): FmaState2 = {
165	    val s2 = Wire(new FmaState2)
166	
167	    // Propagate special flags:
168	    // - NaN if product is NaN or inc is NaN
169	    // - Inf if product is Inf and inc is not NaN (and not Inf-Inf which is NaN)
170	    val resultIsNan = s1.prodIsNan || s1.incIsNan ||
171	                      (s1.prodIsInf && s1.incIsInf && (s1.prodSign =/= s1.incSign))
172	    val resultIsInf = !resultIsNan && (s1.prodIsInf || s1.incIsInf)
173	
174	    s2.isNan    := resultIsNan
175	    s2.isInf    := resultIsInf
176	    s2.isZero   := s1.prodIsZero && s1.incIsZero
177	    s2.prodSign := s1.prodSign
178	    s2.incSign  := s1.incSign
179	
180	    // Extended significands to 27 bits (24 + 3 guard/rounding bits)
181	    val prodSig27 = Cat(s1.prodMantissa, 0.U(3.W))  // 27 bits
182	    val incSig27  = Cat(s1.incMantissa,  0.U(3.W))  // 27 bits
183	
184	    // Compare exponents; align the smaller to the larger
185	    val prodExpU = s1.prodExp  // 9 bits (0..511 but actual range 0..254)
186	    val incExpU  = s1.incExp   // 8 bits (0..255)
187	
188	    // Use wide comparison
189	    val prodGtEqInc = prodExpU >= incExpU
190	
191	    val shiftAmt = Wire(UInt(9.W))
192	    shiftAmt := Mux(prodGtEqInc,
193	      prodExpU - incExpU,
194	      incExpU - prodExpU)
195	
196	    // Clamp shift to 27 (beyond that, the shifted value is negligible)
197	    val shiftClamped = Mux(shiftAmt > 27.U, 27.U, shiftAmt)(4, 0)
198	
199	    val prodAligned = Wire(UInt(27.W))
200	    val incAligned  = Wire(UInt(27.W))
201	    val resultExp   = Wire(UInt(9.W))
202	
203	    when(prodGtEqInc) {
204	      incAligned  := (incSig27 >> shiftClamped)(26, 0)
205	      prodAligned := prodSig27
206	      resultExp   := prodExpU
207	    }.otherwise {
208	      prodAligned := (prodSig27 >> shiftClamped)(26, 0)
209	      incAligned  := incSig27
210	      resultExp   := incExpU
211	    }
212	
213	    // When one operand is zero, use the other's value directly
214	    val finalProdAligned = Mux(s1.prodIsZero, 0.U(27.W), prodAligned)
215	    val finalIncAligned  = Mux(s1.incIsZero,  0.U(27.W), incAligned)
216	
217	    // Determine the result exponent (use the non-zero operand's exponent if one is zero)
218	    val finalResultExp = Wire(UInt(9.W))
219	    when(s1.prodIsZero && !s1.incIsZero) {
220	      finalResultExp := incExpU
221	    }.elsewhen(!s1.prodIsZero && s1.incIsZero) {
222	      finalResultExp := prodExpU
223	    }.otherwise {
224	      finalResultExp := resultExp
225	    }
226

228	    s2.incAligned  := finalIncAligned
229	    s2.resultExp   := finalResultExp

232	  }
